attack_surfaces.description: HELICS messages lack authentication and encryption

assessment_sequence.expected_defensive_response: Logging of discovery events; baseline topology stored for later comparison.
assessment_sequence.name: Topology Discovery

assessment_sequence.expected_defensive_response: Over‑voltage alarm, automatic voltage regulator corrective action, IDS flag for abnormal telemetry.
assessment_sequence.name: Voltage Set‑Point Spoofing – Node650

assessment_sequence.expected_defensive_response: Solver convergence warning, deviation alert in state estimator, possible temporary load shedding.
assessment_sequence.name: Power‑Flow Input Corruption

assessment_sequence.expected_defensive_response: Over‑current protection check, line loading metrics rise, protective relay logs.
assessment_sequence.name: Controlled Load Injection – Bus2

assessment_sequence.expected_defensive_response: Timeout alerts, fallback to local control loops, detection of communication loss.

expected_outcomes.phase_1: Accurate map of communication endpoints and data flow paths for future hardening.
expected_outcomes.phase_2: Verification that voltage regulation alarms trigger within < 1 s and that corrective set‑point actions are logged.
expected_outcomes.phase_3: Demonstration of load‑injection impact on line loading and over‑current relay response times.
expected_outcomes.phase_4: Confirmation that HELICS‑based IDS can detect complete message loss and raise a high‑severity alert.
expected_outcomes.phase_5: Assessment of coordinated protection strategy effectiveness against simultaneous voltage, load, and communication disturbances.

key_vulnerabilities.risk: Message tampering or delay could destabilize coordinated control loops.

key_vulnerabilities.component: Voltage regulation set‑points on critical nodes (Node650, Bus1, Bus2)
key_vulnerabilities.risk: Improper set‑point values can trigger over‑voltage or undervoltage trips.
Corrupted power‑flow inputs may cause solver divergence and cascade warnings.

situation_analysis.overall_state: The simulated IEEE‑13‑bus + 2‑bus system is currently healthy with a perfect health score, but automated analysis flags a high‑severity stability vulnerability (potential oscillations and control system failures). No voltage or power‑flow anomalies are reported yet.

strategic_approach.objective: Perform a staged, defensive‑focused security assessment that validates detection, containment, and recovery capabilities for the identified communication and control‑system weaknesses.
principles: All actions are confined to the isolated simulation environment.
Each test is limited in duration (≤ 5 s) and magnitude to avoid irreversible simulation crashes.
Defensive monitoring (IDS alerts, protection log entries, state‑estimator residuals) is captured for every step.

success_metrics.coverage_percent: Portion of identified vulnerability classes exercised by the test sequence (target ≥ 90 %).
success_metrics.detection_latency_ms: Time from anomaly injection to first IDS/alert entry (target ≤ 500 ms).
success_metrics.false_positive_rate_percent: Number of alerts generated during benign operation / total alerts (target ≤ 2 %).
success_metrics.mitigation_response_time_ms: Time from alert to protective action execution (target ≤ 1 s).
success_metrics.recovery_time_sec: Time to return to healthy state after each test (target ≤ 10 s).
success_metrics.system_stability_score: Post‑test state‑estimator residual norm compared to baseline (target ≤ 1.2× baseline).
